nodes.summary: For a fixed vertex triple $T$, every other triple sharing a pair with $T$ consists of one of the three pairs of $T$ and one further vertex, so there are at most $3n$ of them. The exact count $3(n-3)$ is implicit in Zhao's variance computation for triangles, whose overlap term $\binom n2 (n-2)(n-3)(p^5 - p^6)$ equals $\binom n3 \cdot 3(n-3) \cdot (p^5 - p^6)$.
nodes.title: A triangle shares an edge with at most 3n others

nodes.summary: Two distinct vertex triples meet in at most two vertices, so their pair sets share at most one pair, and together they contain at least $3 + 3 - 1 = 5$ pairs. Hence in $G(n,p)$ two distinct triangles both appear with probability at most $p^5$.
nodes.title: Two triangles sharing an edge span five edges

nodes.summary: For $0 < p \le 1$ and $n \ge 3$, Let $A_T$ be the event that the triple $T$ spans a triangle and $\mu = \binom n3 p^3$ the expected number of triangles. Triangles without a common edge are independent, so the dependency graph joins triples sharing a pair. A dependent pair spans at least five edges, so $\Pr[A_T \cap A_{T'}] \le p^5$, and each triple has at most $3n$ dependent partners; hence…
nodes.title: Second moment bound for triangles in G(n, p)

nodes.summary: For every $p \in [0, 1]$, the expected number of triangles: each of the $\binom n3$ vertex triples spans a triangle with probability $p^3$, and the union bound adds these up.
nodes.title: First moment bound for triangles in G(n, p)

nodes.summary: Two distinct vertex triples are adjacent when they share a pair of vertices, that is, when the corresponding triangles of $K_n$ share an edge. Triangles that share no edge are determined by disjoint sets of edges of $G(n, p)$ and are independent, so this is a dependency graph for the events "$T$ spans a triangle" in the sense of the second moment method.
nodes.title: Dependency graph of the triangle events

nodes.summary: Let $p_n \in [0, 1]$ with $n p_n \to \infty$. Then For $n \ge 3$ one has $\binom n3 \ge n^3/162$, so the second moment bound gives $\Pr[\text{triangle-free}] \le 162/(np_n)^3 + 486/(np_n) \to 0$. Together with the first half, $1/n$ is a threshold function for containing a triangle in the sense of Zhao's Definition 4.10.
nodes.title: Triangles appear above the threshold 1/n

nodes.summary: Let $p_n \in [0, 1]$ with $n p_n \to 0$. Then Indeed the probability is at most $\binom n3 p_n^3 \le (n p_n)^3$.
nodes.title: Triangles are absent below the threshold 1/n

nodes.summary: The three-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$; there are $\binom n3$ of them. Each is the vertex set of one possible triangle of a graph on $n$ vertices, and its three pairs are the triangle's edges.
nodes.title: Vertex triples

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.
